annotations.label: Second-order logic (as extension of first-order logic)

anchor.snippet: second-order logic is an extension of first-order logic

annotations.note: Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language` framework formalizes only first-order logic; no second-order extension exists.

annotations.label: Second-order quantification over relations

anchor.snippet: second-order logic, in addition, quantifies over relations

annotations.note: No second-order relation-quantification construct in Mathlib's model theory library.

annotations.label: Law of excluded middle as a second-order sentence

anchor.snippet: says that for every formula P , and every individual x , either Px is true or not( Px ) is true

annotations.note: LEM as a second-order sentence has no formalization; Mathlib's classical `em` is a metalogical axiom, not an SO sentence.

annotations.label: Domain of discourse

anchor.snippet: The domain is a set over which individual elements may be quantified.

annotations.note: Mathlib has first-order `Language.Structure` carriers but no second-order domain-of-discourse formalization.

annotations.label: Quantifying over individuals (first-order)

anchor.snippet: we can take an atomic sentence like Cube( b ) and obtain a quantified sentence

annotations.note: An illustrative example, not a formal statement to formalize.

annotations.label: Quantifying over predicates (second-order)

anchor.snippet: is not a sentence of first-order logic, but this is a legitimate sentence of second-order logic

annotations.note: No SO predicate-quantification syntax exists in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Set of cubes and tetrahedrons

anchor.snippet: the existence of this set can be asserted in second-order logic as

annotations.note: SO comprehension example; no SO framework in Mathlib.

annotations.label: No dodecahedrons in the set

anchor.snippet: the set of all cubes and tetrahedrons does not contain any dodecahedrons

annotations.note: SO illustrative example; no SO logic in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Ancestor relation via second-order quantification

anchor.snippet: every set of people containing y and closed under the Parent relation contains x

annotations.note: SO definition of ancestor closure is not formalized; Mathlib's `Relation.TransGen` is a Lean-level analogue, not an SO formula.

annotations.label: No second-order variables for properties of predicates

anchor.snippet: we don't have variables for properties of predicates

annotations.note: A restriction of SO syntax; no SO syntax formalization exists in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Equality (Leibniz's law)

anchor.snippet: Objects are defined to be equal when they share all properties

annotations.note: Lean's `Eq` is built-in but the SO Leibniz definition `∀P, Px ↔ Py` is not a formal statement in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Second-order induction axiom

anchor.snippet: it can be expressed concisely as a single axiom

annotations.note: Lean's `Nat.rec` gives induction, but the SO Peano induction axiom quantifying over all sets is not formalized as an SO sentence.

annotations.label: Sort of set (unary relation) variables

anchor.snippet: A sort of variables that range over sets of individuals.

annotations.note: No SO variable sorts in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Sort of k-ary relation variables

anchor.snippet: there is a sort of variables that ranges over all k -ary relations on the individuals

annotations.note: No SO variable sorts formalized.

annotations.label: Sort of k-ary function variables

anchor.snippet: there is a sort of variables that ranges over all functions taking k elements of the domain and returning a single element of the domain

annotations.note: No SO function-variable sort in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Sentence in second-order logic

anchor.snippet: a well-formed formula with no free variables

annotations.note: Mathlib has `FirstOrder.Language.Sentence` for FO but no SO analog.

annotations.label: Function variables reducible to relation variables

anchor.snippet: an n -ary function variable can be represented by a relation variable of arity n +1

annotations.note: SO metatheoretic reduction; not formalized.

annotations.label: Weak second-order logic (WSO)

anchor.snippet: Weak second-order logic (WSO) is a restriction of second-order logic in which only quantification over finite sets is allowed

annotations.note: WSO is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Monadic second-order logic (MSO)

anchor.snippet: Monadic second-order logic (MSO) is a restriction of second-order logic in which only quantification over unary relations

annotations.note: MSO is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Full second-order logic

anchor.snippet: The second-order logic without these restrictions is sometimes called full second-order logic

annotations.note: No SO logic (full or otherwise) exists in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Decidability of the MSO theory of the infinite binary tree (S2S)

anchor.snippet: The MSO theory of the complete infinite binary tree ( S2S ) is decidable

annotations.note: Rabin's S2S decidability is not in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Undecidability of full second-order logic over infinite domains

anchor.snippet: can interpret the true second-order arithmetic and is thus undecidable

annotations.note: Undecidability of true SO arithmetic is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: First-order formula within second-order logic

anchor.snippet: A formula in second-order logic is said to be of first-order

annotations.note: SO-fragment classification not formalized.

annotations.label: Existential second-order formula

anchor.snippet: formula is one additionally having some existential quantifiers over second-order variables

annotations.note: ESO syntax not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Existential second-order logic (ESO)

anchor.snippet: The fragment of second-order logic consisting only of existential second-order formulas is called existential second-order logic

annotations.note: ESO not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Universal second-order logic

anchor.snippet: is defined dually, it is called universal second-order logic

annotations.note: Universal SO not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Higher fragments defined by mutual recursion

anchor.snippet: More expressive fragments are defined for any k > 0 by mutual recursion

annotations.note: SO fragment hierarchy not formalized.

annotations.label: Standard (full) semantics

anchor.snippet: In standard semantics, also called full semantics, the quantifiers range over all sets or functions

annotations.note: Standard SO semantics not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Full model

anchor.snippet: A model with this condition is called a full model

annotations.note: SO full model not defined in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Henkin semantics

anchor.snippet: Leon Henkin (1950) defined an alternative kind of semantics for second-order and higher-order theories

annotations.note: Henkin semantics not formalized.

annotations.label: Henkin's completeness and compactness theorem

anchor.snippet: Henkin proved that Gödel's completeness theorem and compactness theorem

annotations.note: The SO-with-Henkin-semantics completeness theorem is not in Mathlib (only the FO compactness `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.isSatisfiable_iff_isFinitelySatisfiable`).

annotations.label: Henkin models as disguised first-order models (Lindström)

anchor.snippet: Lindström's theorem imports that Henkin models are just disguised first-order models

annotations.note: Lindström's theorem is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Non-standard interpretations as a consequence of Gödel's incompleteness theorem

anchor.snippet: a necessary consequence of Gödel's incompleteness theorem

annotations.note: Gödel incompleteness is not in Mathlib; the SO corollary is likewise absent.

annotations.label: Additive inverse expressible in first-order logic

anchor.snippet: one can assert in first-order logic the existence of an additive inverse of each real number

annotations.note: The FO sentence about additive inverses is not written down in Mathlib's `ModelTheory` API.

annotations.label: Least-upper-bound property

anchor.snippet: one needs second-order logic to assert the least-upper-bound property for sets of real numbers, which states that every bounded, nonempty set of real numbers has a supremum

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes the LUB property Lean-internally via `ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder` (and `Real` is an instance), but not as a second-order sentence.

annotations.label: Categoricity of ordered fields satisfying the LUB property

anchor.snippet: Any ordered field that satisfies this property is isomorphic to the real number field

annotations.note: Mathlib's `inducedOrderRingIso` proves any two conditionally complete linear ordered fields are canonically isomorphic, giving categoricity of the reals.

annotations.label: LUB property not first-order expressible

anchor.snippet: Thus the least-upper-bound property cannot be expressed by any set of sentences in first-order logic

annotations.note: This metalogical non-expressibility result is not formalized.

annotations.label: Real-closed fields share first-order theory with the reals

anchor.snippet: every real-closed field satisfies the same first-order sentences in the signature

annotations.note: Mathlib has `IsRealClosed` but not the model-completeness / Tarski FO-elementary-equivalence statement.

annotations.label: Finiteness expressible in second-order logic

anchor.snippet: use the sentence that says that every surjective function from the domain to itself is injective

annotations.note: SO characterization of finiteness is not formalized in Mathlib; the Lean-level fact `Finite.injective_of_surjective` exists but is not the SO sentence.

annotations.label: Countable cardinality expressible in second-order logic

anchor.snippet: there is a bijection between every two infinite subsets of the domain

annotations.note: SO characterization of countability is not in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Finiteness/countability not first-order expressible

anchor.snippet: it is not possible to characterize finiteness or countability, respectively, in first-order logic

annotations.note: This FO non-expressibility metatheorem is not formalized.

annotations.label: ESO fragment more expressive than first-order logic

anchor.snippet: Certain fragments of second-order logic like ESO are also more expressive than first-order logic

annotations.note: No ESO/FO comparative expressiveness in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Deductive system

anchor.snippet: A deductive system for a logic is a set of inference rules and logical axioms

annotations.note: No abstract SO deductive system formalized (Mathlib's FO proof calculus is `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.Proof`).

annotations.label: No deductive system complete for standard semantics

anchor.snippet: none can be complete for the standard semantics

annotations.note: SO incompleteness metatheorem not formalized.

annotations.label: Weakest deductive system for second-order logic

anchor.snippet: The weakest deductive system that can be used consists of a standard deductive system for first-order logic

annotations.note: SO deductive system (with comprehension) not formalized.

annotations.label: Soundness of comprehension and choice axioms

anchor.snippet: These axioms are sound for standard second-order semantics

annotations.note: Comprehension/choice soundness for SO is not formalized.

annotations.label: Attempted reduction to a two-sorted first-order theory

anchor.snippet: One might attempt to reduce the second-order theory of the real numbers, with full second-order semantics, to the first-order theory

annotations.note: This meta-example is not a formal statement to formalize.

annotations.label: Löwenheim–Skolem construction of internal numbers/sets

anchor.snippet: That theorem implies that there is some countably infinite subset of the real numbers

annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes downward Löwenheim–Skolem for FO languages, from which the countable-elementary-substructure claim would follow, though the reals application isn't spelled out.

annotations.label: Internal numbers fail the full least-upper-bound axiom

anchor.snippet: implies that that set does not satisfy the full least-upper-bound axiom

annotations.note: This corollary about SO-LUB failure on the countable substructure isn't formalized.

annotations.label: Uniqueness of the Archimedean complete ordered field

anchor.snippet: This follows from the classical theorem that there is only one Archimedean complete ordered field

annotations.note: `inducedOrderRingIso` gives the canonical iso between any two conditionally complete linear ordered fields, i.e. uniqueness of ℝ.

annotations.label: Second-order theory of the reals not reducible to first-order theory

anchor.snippet: This shows that the second-order theory of the real numbers cannot be reduced to a first-order theory

annotations.note: This non-reducibility metatheorem is not formalized.

annotations.label: Continuum-hypothesis-dependent second-order theory

anchor.snippet: There is a finite second-order theory whose only model is the real numbers if the continuum hypothesis holds

annotations.note: The CH-conditional SO categoricity example is not formalized.

annotations.label: No sound, complete, effective deductive system for full second-order logic

anchor.snippet: It is a corollary of Gödel's incompleteness theorem that there is no deductive system

annotations.note: SO incompleteness is not formalized in Mathlib.

annotations.label: Henkin's completeness theorem for Henkin semantics

anchor.snippet: Henkin proved that the standard deductive system for first-order logic is sound, complete, and effective for second-order logic with Henkin semantics

annotations.note: Mathlib has FO compactness but not the Henkin-semantics SO completeness theorem.

annotations.label: Compactness and Löwenheim–Skolem fail for full models

anchor.snippet: do not hold for full models of second-order logic

annotations.note: The failure of compactness/L–S for full-semantics SO is not formalized.

annotations.label: Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem

anchor.snippet: REG (the regular languages ) is the set of languages definable by monadic, second-order formulas

annotations.note: Mathlib has `RegularExpressions`/`DFA`/`NFA` but no MSO=REG theorem.

annotations.label: Fagin's theorem

anchor.snippet: NP is the set of languages definable by existential, second-order formulas

annotations.note: Grep for `Fagin` returns no hits; NP=ESO is not in Mathlib.

annotations.label: co-NP characterized by universal second-order formulas

anchor.snippet: co-NP is the set of languages definable by universal, second-order formulas

annotations.note: Descriptive-complexity theorems are absent from Mathlib.

annotations.label: PH characterized by second-order formulas

anchor.snippet: PH is the set of languages definable by second-order formulas

annotations.note: PH descriptive characterization not in Mathlib.

annotations.label: PSPACE characterized by second-order formulas with transitive closure

anchor.snippet: PSPACE is the set of languages definable by second-order formulas with an added transitive closure operator

annotations.note: PSPACE descriptive characterization not in Mathlib.

annotations.label: EXPTIME characterized by second-order formulas with least fixed point

anchor.snippet: EXPTIME is the set of languages definable by second-order formulas with an added least fixed point operator

annotations.note: EXPTIME descriptive characterization not in Mathlib.

annotations.label: PH = PSPACE consequence for transitive closure expressiveness

anchor.snippet: if PH = PSPACE , then adding a transitive closure operator to second-order logic would not make it any more expressive

annotations.note: This complexity-conditional statement is not formalized.
